$comment: CANONICAL SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Hermes/iroh realtime wire protocol. Frame types and wire constants are hand-mirrored across Swift (OpenBurnBarCore), Kotlin (android/openburnbar-iroh-relay), TypeScript (services/hermes-realtime-relay), and Rust (crates/openburnbar-iroh). Edit HERE and run `node codegen.mjs`; CI parity gate fails if any language drifts from this file. See README.md.

protocol.doc: version: frame schema version carried in every HermesRealtimeRelayFrame. realtimeCapability: advertised in the host.register frame for the WebSocket/relay path. irohCapability: advertised by the Mac so iOS confirms iroh-transport awareness before binding requests to the iroh stream. alpn: QUIC ALPN shared by Mac + iOS + Android; bumping it is the clean cross-platform upgrade boundary. maxFrameBytes: inbound length-prefix ceiling (512 KiB). lengthPrefix: a 4-byte big-endian u32 prefix precedes each JSON frame on the wire (matches the Rust crate's to_be_bytes writer).

groups.title: Session + chat multiplexing
groups.doc: The original Hermes request/response multiplexing frames. These are the ONLY frames the Cloud Run WebSocket relay (services/hermes-realtime-relay) validates and routes; the relay is a dumb chat multiplexer. Every other group is peer-to-peer over iroh and never touches the relay.

groups.title: Signal session transport
groups.doc: Device-to-device Signal Double Ratchet ciphertext carried over the iroh relay stream. The opaque ciphertext bytes ride the top-level signalSessionCiphertextB64 field so the transport stays protocol-aware but crypto-agnostic.

groups.title: Mercury media
groups.doc: Mercury media rollout (plans/2026-05-15-mercury-media-master-plan.md, docs/HERMES_MEDIA_TRANSPORT.md). Older peers skip unknown frame types on the chat stream, so adding cases here is forward-compatible. iroh-only.

groups.title: Computer Use control plane
groups.doc: Computer Use control plane (plans/2026-05-16-computer-use-master-plan.md). Same forward-compatibility contract as the media frames: older peers skip unknown control frame types. iroh-only.

groups.title: Remote Unlock
groups.doc: Human-only Mac unlock lane. These frames are kept deliberately separate from Computer Use so agents can never consume credential input. iroh-only.

groups.title: System Permission Concierge
groups.doc: System Permission Concierge (Phase 14). The Mac emits status frames when a tool failure is classified as a TCC denial; the phone replies with a signed request asking the Mac to surface the right native prompt / System Settings deep link. Both frames are forward-compatible. iroh-only.

groups.title: War Room — the Wire
groups.doc: The Wire: the encrypted Mac⇄Mac lane for War Room fleet orchestration (plans/2026-08-17-war-room-master-plan.md). Entitlement-gated to Pro/Ultra and fail-closed — a peer that cannot prove an active war_wire_grant answers war.denied and the dispatcher falls back to the Firestore relay. iroh-only; the dialing Mac uses the transport's outbound connect() rather than accept-only host mode.

frames.doc: Host announces itself and its capabilities to the relay.
Server-originated readiness signal to a registered host.
Client opens a request; carries the encrypted operation payload.
Client cancels an in-flight request.
Host streams one response chunk (sse/data/error).
Host signals the response stream is complete.
Host signals a terminal error for the request.
Keep-alive ping. Either role may send.
Keep-alive pong. Either role may send.
Signal Double Ratchet ciphertext; dispatched by the top-level message-type integer. Opaque to the transport.
Media stream-class negotiation.
Advertise a content-addressed media blob.
Acknowledge a media blob advertisement.
Mercury Phase 8: iOS-initiated mirror request. Rides the existing media.control stream; no new ALPN.
Mac ack of a mirror request.
Stop an active mirror.
Select which display to mirror.
iOS outbound presence heartbeat.
Invite the peer to a media call.
Acknowledge a media call invite.
Receiver -> encoder acknowledgement for a VideoToolbox LTR token carried on a decoded MediaFrame v2 video frame. Inert for v1 peers; only participates after both peers negotiate v2.

Encoded OpenBurnBarMedia.MediaFrame bytes over the long-lived media.control stream after a mirror request is accepted. The payload's streamClass identifies the logical receiver (media.screen.video, control.surface.frame, etc.).
Computer Use control-plane classification frame.
Agent Watch action-log entry.
Signed phone-control input intent. Security-relevant: carries the agent's intended input action.
Request human approval for a control action.
Human approval response for a control action.
Request a phone-authenticated grant bound to one exact Computer Use session intent.
Request an agent capability grant.
Receipt for an agent capability grant.
Request clipboard contents.
Clipboard contents response.
A control action was denied.
Identify the agent's current context target.
Open a remote-unlock session.
Remote-unlock session state update.
Human unlock input (keystrokes). Never consumable by agents.
Credential material for remote unlock. Security-critical: human-only lane.
Result of a remote-unlock attempt.
A remote-unlock attempt was denied.
Phone asks the Mac to surface the right native TCC prompt / System Settings deep link.
Mac reports a TCC denial classification back to the phone.
Dialing Mac announces its bodyId, protocol capabilities, and the war_wire_grant it is claiming.
Dialed Mac accepts the Wire session and returns its own bodyId and capabilities.
A body pushes its current fleet-visible state (presence, Hermes state, load) to its Wire peer.
Route a unit of work to this body. Carries the sealed mission payload plus the OriginatorRef the Command Board's STARTED BY column renders.
Dispatch accepted and queued; carries the run id the stream frames reference.
Incremental output for an accepted dispatch, streamed back to the dispatching Mac.
Terminal frame for a dispatched run; carries the final status.
Fail-closed refusal: no active grant, entitlement below Pro, or war_room_kill_switch engaged. The dispatcher falls back to the Firestore relay.
